analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 795-1694). The PR's changes (head lines 1804-1810 and 2148, per file_changes) fall outside these excerpts. The patch excerpt shows only documentation changes: `darkbloom update` now asks the `darkbloom cluster` service supervisor to restart into the installed release together with the other Mac after the pair drained, and the `auto_update` row mentions the pair's coordinated update. No code, configuration defaults or controls change in the supplied evidence. Nothing here changes a trust boundary or invalidates a threat-model assumption, and I found no regression to report.

The base text I examined covers sandbox setup, add-on hold commands, stop/restart, status and doctor. It documents existing behavior, including TB-012/TB-013 (add-on hold socket, installer download over TLS with no CLI-side script verification, T-061) and the T-041 prefix cache. Its content is unchanged by this PR.

Remaining questions for integration: the new cluster-coordinated update restart is implemented in UpdateCommand.swift (`ClusterServiceUpdateRequest`), which is not in the supplied evidence. The cluster peer (second Mac) and the supervisor IPC are not covered by any current threat-model boundary. A later pass should check three things: whether the peer-to-peer and supervisor update-request channels are authenticated; whether the update path still verifies bundle, binary and metallib hashes before replacing the binary; and whether a cluster peer could trigger forced drains or restarts. The threat model may also need a new boundary or threat for cluster coordination. This is flagged as unverified, not as a finding. Because the changed documentation hunks were truncated and implementation files are absent, deeper review is warranted.
